reading.body:
Hakeem Jeffries received at least $33,000 in PAC contributions from AI and technology companies between June 2025 and August 2026, alongside four recorded votes on AI-related bills.

The contributions come from a consistent set of donors: Amazon, Microsoft, Oracle, Google, Meta, and Intel. Amazon gave twice, Microsoft twice, Oracle twice. The amounts are small by federal standards, ranging from $2,500 to $5,000, and they arrive steadily rather than clustering around any single vote. The four recorded votes all passed on motions to suspend the rules, a procedure reserved for uncontroversial legislation. The data does not identify what H.R. 7757, H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770, or S. 146 actually contain, so no connection between the money and the votes can be drawn from this record alone.

What the data does show is that the same companies building and operating AI infrastructure are financially present in the political record of a senior legislator. Intel's contribution is notable because Intel is a chip manufacturer, and chips are the physical substrate of AI compute. Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Meta are the largest buyers and operators of that compute. Oracle is a major cloud and data center provider. The donor list reads as a roster of firms whose AI ambitions depend on buildings, power, and silicon.

The record does not establish causation, coordination, or influence. It does not show what Jeffries did in response to any contribution, and it does not show whether the votes related to AI at all. The four news stories that name him suggest he is part of the broader AI policy conversation, but the data here cannot say in what capacity. What it can say is that the money is real, the votes are recorded, and both are a matter of public filing.
